attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation does not prove the Yang-Mills analytic input that reflected Wilson collar collapse produces either no multiplicative anomaly or only a rank-one boundary Gram anomaly. Balaban-style compactness and fixed-collar convergence do not by themselves exclude a nontrivial boundary Hilbert sector generated by coincident reflected hairpins. The missing estimate is \(C_\partial=0\), equivalently \(K=0\), for the connected boundary OPE of mixed reflected Wilson products in the locked observable algebra.
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity: for every cutoff \((a,L)\), every positive-time gauge-invariant finite family, and coefficients \(c_i\), the quadratic form \(Q_{a,L}=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i,F_j)\) is nonnegative.

Restrict first to a fixed collar \(F_i^\delta\subset\{t>\delta\}\). The RG-to-OS topology is assumed to control each reflected matrix entry, so \(S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta)\to N^\delta_{ij}\). Since the positive semidefinite cone of finite matrices is closed, \(N^\delta\ge0\). This part is valid and essentially formal.

Let \(\delta\downarrow0\). Decompose the difference between the collar limit and the intended boundary-trace matrix as \(N=M+A\) or, after eliminating additive positive contacts, as \(N=B\circ M\). Diagonal trace continuity sets \(A_{ii}=0\) and \(B_{ii}=1\).
For additive positive \(A\), Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(|A_{ij}|^2\le A_{ii}A_{jj}=0\), hence \(A=0\). Therefore positive additive contacts cannot be the remaining obstruction.

For multiplicative \(B\), recovering the intended same-theory matrix requires applying the entrywise reciprocal Schur multiplier: \(M=B^{[-1]}\circ N\). To preserve positivity for arbitrary finite collar matrices, \(B^{[-1]}\) must be positive semidefinite by the Schur product theorem criterion.

Assume the anomaly is itself a normalized boundary Gram matrix, \(B\ge0\), \(B_{ii}=1\). For every two-by-two principal minor, \(B\ge0\) gives \(|B_{ij}|\le1\), while \(B^{[-1]}\ge0\) gives \(|1/B_{ij}|\le1\), so \(|B_{ij}|=1\). A normalized Gram matrix with all pairwise correlations of modulus one has all boundary vectors collinear, hence \(B_{ij}=u_i\overline{u_j}\) and \(K_{ik;jl}=0\).

If \(B_{ij}=u_i\overline{u_j}\), then \(B^{[-1]}_{ij}=\overline{u_i}u_j\) and \(M=D^*ND\) for a diagonal unitary/congruence \(D\). Thus positivity transfers without changing the theory. If any normalized off-diagonal has modulus below one, the reciprocal multiplier has an indefinite two-by-two minor, giving an explicit falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-dimensional Schur/Gram argument is valid, but it is conditional. A full proof still needs: (1) a rigorous construction of the Wilson collar core in the same continuum theory, (2) convergence of all mixed reflected Wilson OS entries as collars collapse, (3) elimination of boundary counterterms and cusp/hairpin renormalizations not already present as diagonal congruences, and (4) OS-density of this core in the target gauge-invariant test algebra.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: boundary Gram triviality for Wilson collar collapse

assumptions: For each fixed collar \(\delta>0\), RG convergence is strong enough that \(S_{a,L}(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta)\to S_\delta(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta)\) for all finite Wilson families and coefficients.
The fixed-collar continuum matrices \(N^\delta_{ij}=S_\delta(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta)\) are positive semidefinite by closed-cone transfer of regulated reflection positivity.
After additive contact terms are removed or shown to vanish, the collar-collapse limit has the form \(N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}\), where \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\) is the intended same-theory OS matrix.
The anomaly kernel \(B\) is normalized by diagonal trace continuity, \(B_{ii}=1\), and is positive as a boundary Gram matrix of possible hairpin boundary states.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms \(S_{a,L}\) on a fixed gauge-invariant test algebra, with Wilson collar representatives \(F_i^\delta\subset\{t>\delta\}\) and finite OS matrices obtained after RG continuum passage at fixed \(\delta>0\).

target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions \(S\) on the full locked gauge-invariant algebra, including Wilson observables whose supports have valid boundary traces at the reflection plane.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, mediated by convergence of every finite reflected quadratic form and by a collar-collapse map \(F_i^\delta\to F_i\).

same-theory condition: the collar limit may only implement diagonal congruences already included in the chosen renormalization of the locked observable algebra; no pair-dependent boundary state, cusp factor, or boundary counterterm may change the OS matrix entries.

equations.label: fixed-collar OS matrix
equations.valid_when: The observable supports are separated from the reflection plane by \(\delta>0\), the regulated lattice reflection positivity is available, and RG convergence controls this finite reflected probe.

equations.label: multiplicative boundary anomaly
equations.valid_when: Additive boundary contacts have vanished or been separated, and collar collapse is encoded by a normalized pair factor on the same Wilson core.

equations.label: reciprocal Schur transfer
equations.valid_when: Every \(B_{ij}\neq0\) and the intended matrix is recovered from the collar matrix without changing the observable algebra.

equations.label: rank-one obstruction test
equations.valid_when: The bridge is required to be valid as a Schur-positive operation on all finite OS matrices generated by the locked core.

equations.label: logarithmic cross-ratio
equations.valid_when: A consistent branch of the logarithm is chosen on a nonzero finite anomaly matrix; \(K=0\) is equivalent to factorization \(B_{ij}=u_i\overline{u_j}\) locally.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find two reflected Wilson hairpins with normalized boundary Gram entry \(B_{12}=r\), \(0<|r|<1\). Taking the positive collar model \(N=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), the recovered target matrix \(M=B^{[-1]}\circ N=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/r\\1/\overline r&1\end{pmatrix}\) has determinant \(1-|r|^{-2}<0\). This is a concrete falsifier of universal same-theory transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the last non-formal part of the reflection-positivity bridge. The closed-cone argument proves positivity of collar matrices; the lemma says that same-theory positivity at the reflection plane is preserved exactly when the Wilson boundary anomaly is only a diagonal congruence, i.e. no nontrivial boundary Hilbert sector is created.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Boundary Gram Triviality Criterion. Fix the locked gauge-invariant Wilson core and let \(F_i^\delta\) be reflected collar representatives of continuum observables \(F_i\) approaching the reflection plane. Suppose the fixed-collar OS matrices have a continuum limit and the remaining collar-collapse anomaly is multiplicative, normalized, and represented by a positive boundary Gram kernel \(B_{ij}=\langle b_i,b_j\rangle\) with \(B_{ii}=1\). Then the passage from the positive collar-limit matrices \(N=B\circ M\) to the intended same-theory OS matrices \(M\) is valid for every finite family only if \(B\) has rank one on every finite family. Equivalently, the logarithmic cross-ratio \(K_{ik;jl}\) vanishes and the boundary Hilbert sector generated by reflected Wilson hairpins is one-dimensional. Any non-rank-one \(B\), for example \(|B_{12}|<1\), is a same-theory falsifier, not merely a removable normalization.

assumptions: The additive defect is a Hermitian positive semidefinite matrix on each finite OS family.
Each diagonal contact vanishes because the individual Wilson observable has a same-theory collar trace.
The finite OS matrix entries are evaluated in one fixed gauge-invariant test algebra, without adding a reflection-plane boundary observable.
definitions: Boundary contact matrix: the finite matrix \(A_{ij}\) obtained as the residual difference between the collar-limit OS entry and the intended boundary-trace OS entry after single-observable renormalizations are fixed.
Diagonal trace continuity: \(S(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_i^\delta)\to S(\Theta F_i,F_i)\) for each Wilson core observable in the same renormalization convention.
Positive boundary contact: \(\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j A_{ij}\ge0\) for every finite coefficient vector \(c\).

equations.label: additive contact split
equations.valid_when: The collar limit exists entrywise and the defect is additive rather than multiplicative.

equations.label: PSD zero diagonal implication
equations.valid_when: The boundary contact matrix is positive semidefinite; this is just Cauchy-Schwarz in the contact Hilbert seminorm.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Produce a mixed additive Wilson contact with \(A_{ii}=A_{jj}=0\) but \(A_{ij}\neq0\). Such an example is a falsifier of positive boundary-contact compatibility, so the proof would have to treat an indefinite boundary defect rather than a harmless positive one.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This removes one apparent obstruction from the branch: positive additive contacts do not create a hidden mixed anomaly once diagonal trace continuity is valid. The only durable obstruction is multiplicative nonfactorization or an indefinite contact term.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Positive additive boundary contacts vanish under diagonal trace continuity. If the collar-collapse defect has the additive form \(N=M+A\), and \(A\) is a positive semidefinite boundary contact matrix with \(A_{ii}=0\) for all locked observables, then \(A=0\). Thus a surviving mixed additive contact must either violate positivity of the boundary contact form or violate diagonal same-theory trace continuity.

assumptions: The limiting Schwinger functions are distributionally continuous on the mirror-smooth local core.
The Wilson core satisfies the boundary Gram triviality criterion on every finite family.
The OS seminorm completion does not identify a different observable algebra from the one used in the regulated theory.
definitions: Mirror-smooth local core: gauge-invariant local composite observables smeared by smooth test functions that are flat or have controlled traces at the reflection plane.
Wilson collar core: finite linear combinations of renormalized Wilson observables with supports initially in \(t>\delta\), equipped with collar maps \(T_\delta F\to F\).
OS-density: every positive-time gauge-invariant observable is approximable in the OS seminorm induced by the limiting Schwinger functions by elements from the union of the local and Wilson cores.

equations.label: trace modulus for extension
equations.valid_when: The collar trace maps are Cauchy in the OS seminorm and the chosen core is dense for the same-theory OS completion.

equations.label: core-to-completion positivity
equations.valid_when: The quadratic form is closed in the OS seminorm topology generated by the limiting Schwinger functions.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If Wilson observables needed for the Yang-Mills algebra are not OS-dense after imposing the collar trace condition, positivity may be proved only for a strict subtheory.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma packages the final promotion path: prove positivity on a dense core, prove the boundary anomaly is trivial there, then use OS closure to reach the target continuum theory.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Dense Wilson-core extension lemma. Suppose a mirror-smooth local core and a Wilson collar core are OS-dense in the locked gauge-invariant test algebra, fixed-collar positivity is valid, additive contacts vanish, and the multiplicative anomaly has zero logarithmic cross-ratio on the Wilson core. Then OS positivity extends from collars to the full continuum Schwinger functions without reintroducing positivity by hand.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this route if a controlled Wilson hairpin calculation gives \(|B_{ij}|<1\), nonzero \(K\), or a required boundary counterterm not expressible as a diagonal congruence in the locked observable algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge if one proves, on an OS-dense Wilson core, that all reflected hairpin boundary Gram matrices are rank one and all additive positive contacts vanish, while RG convergence remains valid for the corresponding finite reflected quadratic forms.
control_decision.reason: The branch has a sharp conditional bridge with a finite-dimensional proof and a precise analytic gap. This is substantive progress: the obstruction has been reduced to computing or bounding a boundary Gram/cross-ratio invariant for mixed Wilson collar collapse.

dependency_updates.description: The fixed-collar part is now separated as a valid closed-cone theorem. The remaining analytic dependency is not generic OS closure but boundary Gram triviality for reflected Wilson collar collapse.

The same-theory algebra must lock in the Wilson renormalization before the collar limit. Pair-dependent boundary factors are disallowed unless they reduce to diagonal congruences already present in the chosen observable definitions.

The topology must dominate finite reflected OS probes first at fixed collar and then through a trace modulus at the reflection plane. Ordinary distributional convergence on local composites is insufficient for mixed Wilson hairpins.
Prove that the boundary states generated by reflected Wilson hairpin collapse are all collinear, equivalently \(B\) is rank one, \(K=0\), or the connected boundary covariance \(C_\partial\) vanishes.

falsifiers: A nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio \(K_{ik;jl}\) for four reflected Wilson hairpins with the same reflection-plane footprint; this is the cleanest multiplicative same-theory falsifier.
A normalized boundary Gram matrix \(B\) with \(B_{ii}=1\) but \(|B_{ij}|<1\) for some mixed Wilson pair, since the reciprocal Schur multiplier is then indefinite.
A boundary Wilson OPE producing a new reflection-plane observable whose coefficient is pair-dependent rather than a diagonal Wilson-loop renormalization.
An indefinite additive contact term with zero diagonal but nonzero mixed entry; this would evade the positive-contact vanishing lemma and signal a deeper failure of the boundary trace model.

RG convergence that is valid for individual Wilson expectations but not for reflected OS matrix entries \(S(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta)\), especially when \(\Theta F_i^\delta\) and \(F_j^\delta\) collide into a hairpin.
Gauge fixing, quotienting, or Wilson-loop renormalization that changes the locked test algebra between cutoff and continuum; positivity might survive, but for the wrong theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 192 converts the remaining obstruction into an exact boundary Gram criterion. The formal reflection-positive closed-cone passage is valid on fixed collars, and positive additive contacts vanish once diagonal trace continuity is known. The only robust same-theory obstruction is a multiplicative boundary Gram factor from reflected Wilson hairpins. If its reciprocal Schur multiplier is to preserve OS positivity, two-by-two minors force the normalized Gram factor to be rank one; equivalently \(K=0\) and no nontrivial boundary Hilbert sector is created. Thus the next Yang-Mills work is no longer to restate reflection positivity, but to prove boundary Gram triviality \(C_\partial=0\) on the locked Wilson core or find a concrete nonrank-one hairpin falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out a model reflected Wilson hairpin pair with identical boundary footprint and different interior shape. Define the normalized anomaly ratio \(B_{12}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}N_{12} /(M_{12}\sqrt{N_{11}N_{22}/(M_{11}M_{22})})\), compute or bound the connected boundary OPE coefficient \(C_\partial(1,2)\), and test whether the logarithmic cross-ratio \(K\) vanishes. The goal is either a proof of collinearity of boundary hairpin states or a concrete nonzero-\(K\) falsifier.
